question.leadin: The continent of Europe is home to many notable seas of the world.
question.text: This sea in eastern Europe names the region containing Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Stockholm, Sweden, lies on the shores of this sea.
question.clue: The defeat of Wendish tribes along this body's southern shores led to the rise of the Viking Age, and the modern Kaliningrad Oblast borders this body.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about German invasions during World War II.
swap.text: Germany invaded this country and Denmark as part of Operation Weserubung. This country was home to German heavy water production and was led by Vidkun Quisling after its surrender.
swap.clue: Another leader of this country served with Josef Terboven and was executed with Albert Hagelin after establishing a fascist government.

question.leadin: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country.
question.text: Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
question.clue: A period of internal clan violence in this country is called the Age of the Sturlungs, and involved this country's great writer of sagas, Snorri Sturluson.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Nystad ended this war in 1721, 12 years after a decisive victory over Charles XII at Poltava ended Sweden's time as a European power.
swap.text: Name this war motivated by one European power's desire for a port city on the Baltic Sea.
swap.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

question.leadin: This leader was killed while leading a cavalry charge at the Battle of Lutzen ["Loot-zen"].
question.text: Name this "Lion of the North," who led the Swedish forces in the Thirty Years War.
question.clue: At the Battle of Lech, also known as the "Battle of Rain," he commanded troops over the Count of Tilly.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Knared ended a war that shares a name with this union.
swap.text: Name this union of Scandinavia first ruled by Eric of Pomerania to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League.
swap.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

question.text: Calvinism failed to gain a foothold in this country as a result of the Synod of Uppsala, which declared Lutheranism the state religion. The followers of Sten Sture the Younger were killed in a "bloodbath" named for this country's capital.
question.clue: This nation was home to a supposed lover of Marie Antoinette, Axel Fersen, who was killed after the overthrow of this nation's ruler Gustav IV.

swap.leadin: The first recorded king of this nation was Gorm the Old, and its flag is said to have fallen from the heavens at a 1219 battle, making it the oldest continually used national standard.
swap.text: Name this Scandinavian nation located primarily on the Jutland peninsula. Its capital is Copenhagen.
swap.clue: This country gained power under Waldemar II in the fourteenth century, and under his descendant Margaret I it became the center of the Kalmar Union.

question.leadin: It arose over the control of the Hanko naval base and was prosecuted by the coalition government of Risto Ryti.
question.text: Name this war which saw the use of the Mannerheim line in an attempt to repel a Soviet invasion.
question.clue: One sniper in this war had 505 confirmed kills, earning him the nickname "White Death".

swap.leadin: These people use a unit of measurement called a poronkusema, which is based on how far a reindeer can move before urinating.
swap.text: Name these people of northern Scandinavia and Russia whose economy traditionally depended on reindeer herding.
swap.answerHtml: Sámi [or Saami; or Sabme; accept Lapplanders but politely inform the person giving the answer that this term is not preferred anymore]
swap.clue: Protests against the construction of the Alta hydroelectric power station strengthened activism for these people's rights and led to the 1989 formation of their first parliament.

question.text: This Norwegian claim, located between the British and Australian claims at 20 degrees West and around 44 degrees East, was named by Roald Amundsen after the wife of King Haakon VII.
question.clue: The Prime Meridian also passes through this Antarctic region. Claimed by Norway, this region is named for the wife of King Haakon VII ["the seventh"], who reigned from 1905 to 1957, and who was also the daughter of King Edward VII ["the seventh"] of Great Britain.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about World War II in Scandinavia.
swap.text: This country fought in the Winter War and the Continuation War against its eastern neighbor, the Soviet Union.
swap.answerHtml: Republic of Finland [or Suomen tasavalta; or Suomi; or Republiken Finland]
swap.clue: Due to the nationalistic drivings of Johan Snellman, this country underwent a namesake language strife in the 1800s. This country won the Battle of Raate Road.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of the good old-fashioned fun of throwing sticks.
question.text: The stick throwing game of skittles originated in a region this country shares with its eastern neighbour. A bat sport invented by a veteran of this country's Civil War was demonstrated when it hosted the 1952 Summer Olympics.
question.clue: Principles surrounding the ethics of human experimentation were codified in a declaration signed in this country, which lends its name to a process in which a small country adopts a larger neighbor's foreign policy prerogatives.

swap.text: The Kalmar Union was founded by this monarch, who ordered that the False Olaf be burned with a necklace of his forged letters as kindling. The Victual Brothers were employed against this "Semiramis of the North" during her siege of Stockholm.
swap.answerHtml: Margaret I of Denmark [accept Margaret Valdemarsdotter; prompt on Margaret]
swap.clue: This ruler, who was often mocked as being "Pantsless" by Albert of Mecklenburg, was the first target of the Victual Brothers, who provided supplies to counteract this ruler's siege of Stockholm.

question.text: Finnish became an official language of administration during an "Age of" this concept in Sweden. That era named for this concept saw increased parliamentary power after the Great Northern War.
question.answerHtml: Age of Liberty [accept frihetstiden or frihet; accept vapauden aika or vapautta]
question.clue: This era follows an era of imperialism called the Stormaktstiden ("STORM-okts-tee-den").

swap.text: A Danish king of this name, the third from the House of Glucksburg and tenth overall, gave a curt reply to Hitler's birthday telegram, which prompted the "Telegram crisis." That king of this name dismissed his government at the end of the Easter Crisis.
swap.clue: In addition to Vilhelm Buhl, another prime minister who served under this king was deposed after failing to call a referendum regarding the return of Flensburg to his country, and that prime minister was named Carl Theodor Zahle.

question.text: Admiral Jellicoe's greatest triumph came at this May 31, 1916, naval engagement that saw the defeat of the German fleet under Reinhard Scheer.
question.clue: The Battle of Dybbol in the Second Schleswig War took place in this region which makes up most of modern-day Denmark. John Jellicoe led British forces at an inconclusive World War I naval battle named for this body of land.

swap.leadin: This erector of the Jelling Stones was the first Danish king to be baptized.
swap.text: Name this unifier of Denmark, the son of Gorm the Old.

question.leadin: He had to deal with revolts in Dalarna and one led by Nils Dacke, and at the Diet of Vasteras, he confiscated the property of Sweden's Catholic Church.
question.text: Name this founder of the Vasa dynasty who signed the Treaty of Malmo with Christian II, thus relieving Sweden of Denmark's rule in the Kalmar Union.

swap.text: Following the Battle of Poltava, Lewanhaupt and Charles adandoned everything leading to this time period of Norwegian history in which the Russians decimated the population of Norway.
swap.answerHtml: The Greater Wrath [accept: isoviha from Will Alston; accept The Great Discord]
